newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks sprint home to end at highs.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks sprint home to end at highs.

text.p: The Australian share market sprinted home to end at its day's high on Wednesday as buyers re-emerged after metal prices firmed overseas and bonds rallied as the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged.
The All Ordinaries index rose 24.1 points to 2252.8.
Brokers said local investors had taken heart from interest rate developments in the U.S. and gold and base metals prices that showed signs of a rebound, at least in the short term.
"You have seen renewed interest in the metals stocks on the back of firmer copper and gold prices," said dealer Martin Angel of Perth-based brokerage Eyres Reed.
"The selldown was overdone and after yesterday's meeting, some investors are back on BHP's side," he said.
Angel noted the unchanged U.S. interest rate scenario, saying that while it may give mixed signals to U.S. investors, local players seemed happy with the Australian implications.
"I'm not sure whether leaving rates unchanged was a good or bad thing, but certainly some people locally are more comfortable that we may come down a touch," he said.
Major mining stocks CRA and BHP led the way in the resources sector. CRA shares closed 43 cents higher at A$18.55 while BHP shares 28 cents to A$16.20.

In the industrials, the big banks soared as the bond market rallied. Commonwealth Bank instalment receipts again took the leading role, climbing more than three percent, but a solid supporting performance came from ANZ Bank which touched a record high of A$7.05 before closing at A$7.04.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
